rules: Spawn the `MqttRunner` that `MqttBroker::new` returns as a task of its own on a device, over `EmbassyNetwork`; the broker connects only while its runner runs, and on compio `MqttBroker::compio` starts the runner itself (MqttBroker page).

Declare the device broker's memory as `static MQTT: ConstStaticCell<MqttState<MESSAGES, PACKET, SUBSCRIPTIONS>> = ConstStaticCell::new(MqttState::new())`, take it once with `MQTT.take()` and pass it to `MqttBroker::new(state, config)` (MqttState page).

Size `MqttState` by its three numbers: `MESSAGES` deliveries held at once, `PACKET` bytes for the largest packet in either direction, and `SUBSCRIPTIONS` open subscriptions; the runner stops reading while every receive buffer is held (MqttState page).

On a device a delivery borrows its topic and payload from the receive buffer its packet arrived in, so a handler reads the payload with `#[derive(Deserialized)]` over `&'a [u8]` and a reply leaves as the bytes of a `#[derive(Serialized)]` type (MqttBroker and Getting started on a device pages).
Keep a device's `MqttConfig` in a `const`: its texts are `&'static str` literals of the firmware (MqttConfig page).

Select the heap variant with the `alloc` feature of the crate, which `compio` implies; a feature of `ruststream` that turns its `alloc` on, such as `json`, needs the crate's `alloc` feature as well (MqttBroker page).
Test a device service on the host with the `testing` feature, declaring a `static` `MqttState` in the test and building the broker over it as the board does (The embedded TestApp page).
Import `ruststream_rust_mqtt::prelude::*` in the file that mounts handlers; it brings the framework's prelude and this crate's descriptors, policy and steps (Components pages).

Subscribe with `MqttTopic` for one topic a publisher can name and `MqttFilter` for a filter with `+` or `#`; a wildcard in an `MqttTopic` is refused when the app starts (MqttTopic and MqttFilter pages).

Name where an `MqttFilter` subscription's retry copies go with `.out_retry(MqttPublish::default()).to("topic")`, and on a device add `.retry_capacity::<N>()` after the mount for `retry_after` (Retry after page).

Expect `AckError::Unsupported` from the settlement of a QoS 0 delivery and from `retry()`, which is `nack(true)`: MQTT has no packet for either, and `drop()` acknowledges (Acknowledgement and Negative acknowledgement pages).

Declare the QoS and retain flag once with `MqttPublish::default().qos(..).retain(..)` at the mount, and change one message with the `.qos(..)` and `.retain(..)` steps of `MqttPublishSteps` (MqttPublish and MqttPublishSteps pages).
Bound a slot `Out<impl Publisher<Options = MqttPublishOptions>, Marker>` in a handler body that takes the `qos` or `retain` step (MqttPublishSteps page).
Spread a topic over replicas with `.shared("group")` on the descriptor, so the server hands each message to one member of the share group (Shared subscription page).

Test a service with the embedded `TestApp` (device) or the compio `TestApp` (host) on the production app, with the `testing` feature, addressing the broker as `tb.broker::<MqttBroker>()` and moving time with `advance` (Testing pages).
Run a live test only for what the in-process transport leaves to the server, gated by `MQTT_TEST_URL`, and start the stand with `just test-brokers` (The live stand page).
